stem: Qasim multiplies $\dfrac{9}{14} \times \dfrac{21}{15}$ and wants to cancel common factors before multiplying.

parts.text: Which claim correctly cancels common factors before multiplying?

options.text: Multiply $9 \times 21$ and $14 \times 15$ first, leaving every common factor uncancelled.
Cancel a common factor $7$ between $21$ and $14$, and a common factor $3$ between $9$ and $15$, then multiply to get $\dfrac{9}{10}$.
Cancel the two numerators $9$ and $21$ with each other before multiplying.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Cancellation pairs a numerator with a denominator that share a factor. Here 21 with 14 (factor 7) and 9 with 15 (factor 3) leave 3/2 × 3/5 = 9/10.

teacher.key_rationale: Cancel 7 between 21 and 14 and 3 between 9 and 15, then multiply to 9/10. Skipping cancellation or cancelling numerator with numerator both miss the product rule.
